python3 << 'PY'
import workcell

TARE = 122.85
TARGET = 250.00
LO, HI = 249.80, 250.20

def net():
    r = workcell.call("scale", "read")
    if not r.ok:
        raise SystemExit(r.text)
    g = r.data["gross_g"]
    n = round(g - TARE, 2)
    print(f"SCALE {g:.2f} NET {n:.2f}")
    return n

r = workcell.call("robot", "pick", "J2")
print(r.text)
r = workcell.call("robot", "place", "platform")
print(r.text)
n = net()
print("empty net", n)

for i in range(4):
    r = workcell.call("robot", "dose", "bulk")
    print("bulk", r.ok, r.text)
n = net()

# coarse until within ~1.2 g below target, leaving room for micro
while n < TARGET - 12.0:
    r = workcell.call("robot", "dose", "coarse")
    print("coarse", r.text)
    n = net()

# if still more than ~0.8 below, one more coarse might be ok if coarse ~10
# but measure uncertainty: if gap > 1.5 use coarse, else fine/micro
while n < TARGET - 1.2:
    # if gap is large use coarse, if medium use fine
    gap = TARGET - n
    if gap > 8:
        kind = "coarse"
    elif gap > 1.2:
        kind = "fine"
    else:
        break
    r = workcell.call("robot", "dose", kind)
    print(kind, r.text)
    n = net()
    if n > HI:
        print("OVERSHOT", n)
        break

# micro approach
while n < LO:
    gap = round(TARGET - n, 2)
    if gap > 0.7:
        kind = "fine"
    else:
        kind = "micro"
    r = workcell.call("robot", "dose", kind)
    print(kind, "gap was", gap, r.text)
    n = net()
    if n > HI:
        print("OVERSHOT", n)
        break

print("FINAL", n)
if LO <= n <= HI:
    r = workcell.call("checkweigher", "check")
    print(r.text, r.data)
else:
    print("NOT IN TOLERANCE")
PY

    print(r.text)
    n = net()
    if n > HI:

        break

# Dosing cell D3 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with a gripper and a dosing head fed from the powder hopper.
- Jar rack: sample jars J1-J3 (empty; each jar's tare is on its barcode label and known to the checkweigher).
- Checkweigher: one weighing platform (readability 0.01 g). `checkweigher check` weighs the jar on the platform,
  subtracts the jar's tare, and prints a PASS label if the net mass is within 250.00 +/- 0.20 g.
  Configuration: /etc/checkweigher/scale.conf.

  robot status                        gripper state, robot time

    r = workcell.call("scale", "read")
    if not r.ok:

while n < TARGET - 1.2:

    gap = TARGET - n
    if gap > 8:

# I'll dose fine one at a time while n < 248.6 (room of 1.6 for a lump)
while n < 248.60:
    n = dose("fine")
    if n > HI:
        print("OVER")
        break

print("SWITCH", n)
# now micro until in range. micro usually 0.1, sometimes lumps 0.7-1.4
while n < LO and n <= HI:
    n = dose("micro")
    if n > HI:
        print("OVER")
        break

print("DONE", n)
r = workcell.call("station", "status")
print(r.text)
if LO <= n <= HI:
    r = workcell.call("checkweigher", "check")
    print(r.text, r.data)
PY
